stemMarkdown: A 80-litre solution contains 40% acid. How many litres of water must be added to dilute it to a 25% acid solution? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The acid stays fixed at $32.00$ litres. For that to be $25\%$ of the solution, the total volume must become $\dfrac{32.00 \times 100}{25} = 128.00$ litres. Water to add $= 128.00 - 80 = 48.0$ litres.
altSolutionMarkdown: Only the solvent changes — anchoring on the unchanged solute is what makes these quick.
